supporting_observations.claim: The supplied records show repeated failed network logons for svc-render on FILE-NWD-01 from 13:31:03 through 13:46:04 UTC, at roughly one-minute intervals.
The failures consistently identify WorkstationName=FILE-NWD-01, source IP 10.40.20.20, LogonType=3, and ProcessId 0xa5c with ProcessName lsass.exe.

The domain-controller records report bad-password status 0xc000006a for svc-render and Kerberos pre-authentication failure status 0x18, consistent with rejected credentials rather than evidence of successful authentication.

The timing and near-minute cadence are consistent with the documented svc-render password rotation at 13:30 UTC followed by a scheduled job continuing to use outdated credentials; the inventory says that job runs and re-authenticates every minute.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records stop at 13:46:04 UTC (T032-00033); they do not cover the remainder of the requested window through 14:20 UTC.
The records show the authentication subsystem process lsass.exe, but do not identify the application or job that initiated each attempt.
These records show failures; they do not establish whether the password rotation occurred or whether any later authentication succeeded.
claims_not_established: That the scheduled password rotation was completed at 13:30 UTC.
That the RenderQueue job's stored credentials were or were not updated.
That no successful logon or other activity occurred elsewhere in the requested 13:20–14:20 UTC window.
That the failures were caused by an attacker rather than stale service credentials.
additional_evidence_needed: For corroboration, check the password-rotation change record and domain-controller account-change audit around 13:30 UTC.
If the cause remains uncertain, inspect RenderQueue/service configuration and application logs on FILE-NWD-01 around the failure period.
Review authentication records from 13:46 through 14:20 UTC to complete the requested window.
